title: Touring from San Antonio, pay and bus troubles in the Depression
summary: Alcorn's band was based in San Antonio, booked by agencies; pay was poor and bus repairs were costly.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Were you living out of Chicago then or New Orleans?

No. Well, this was always my home man. I never really kept up my home then. But I lived in San Antonio at that time. We were working in San Antonio. That was our headquarters. We were down in the out of Spain. And the agencies used to book us, you see. We were going over to West Virginia. We were some time we played. Two nights. A night in the town. Two bands. You see, running. Cab Calloway, Duke. Tom Redden, the only big band.
Do you think you all were well paid back in those days?
I don't know if they were well paid.
No. You could say the fact that it was the Depression and a lot of folks were just not eating.
That's right. But I don't say we were well paid but it wasn't happening.
What would you make on an average night?

Well, you see, we was talking about on the bus. Mm-hmm. First time we try to do some time. We do pretty nice on the night. We run and the bus will really end out. And what? The rear end of the bus jump out. Get all that fixed up. You had nothing but headaches, you know? Oh, man. It was something. Bus out, one of them big old greenhouse bus tires. That's $150. Back in the Depression almost. Man. So, I mean, you see, it was just nothing wasn't. Many guys got disgusted in that out of here.
Some guys went into the professor and doctors and all these things. They just got on for the day.
